label: A thing moves another in some respect only insofar as it is itself in act in…, from causal excess
meaning: Derives the prima via premise that a thing moves only insofar as it is in act. Case split on whether the mover y is the moved x. If distinct: y causes x's being r (OPEN bridge), so y is more r than x (Metaphysics II.1), so y has r in act (quarta via). If y = x: diagonal SELF_MOTION_1 is handled by an OPEN analyst distinct-part premise, not the independent SELF_MOTION_2 of Physics VIII.4-5; by the distinct case p is in act in r, and the whole is in act through its part (OPEN). It does not use STMT-NO-MOVER-MOVES-ITSELF-IN-ITS-RESPECT, which is derived from the conclusion. This answers the self-mover gap that rejected the lead in ATTEMPT-REJECTED-DERIVATION-LEADS-20261107.

strong_version_needed.d5a94eb1-72d2-53e0-9a52-9787b5b61a8d: The frozen proof applies causal comparison at arbitrary r, including the distinct part in its self-motion case, so the esse-only version does not supply those applications. This is current-proof scope, not a minimality claim: distinct-cause possession 2c0b9bd7 could replace the pair of causal comparison and bearer premises in a new sibling; that sibling remains unregistered and unchecked.
